intro: Gentlemen, Gameweek 1 is done and the table has opinions already. Asher scored 80 and leads by 21 from Ben on 59. Jonny is third on 55. Brahmes scored 28 and sits last, 52 points behind the leader. Louie and Jack are level on 42, as are Jamie and Josh on 37. Brentford beat Spurs 3-0, which will not have helped Brahmes, who owns Kinsky, Kudus and Sávio. Newcastle and Liverpool drew 2-2 and Man Utd lost 2-0 at Hull. Nobody has moved yet, because nobody could.
motw: Asher, 80 points. De Cuyper scored 17 on his own, with a goal, an assist, a clean sheet and 2 bonus. Gakpo added 12 and White 11. Three players in the team of the week came from one squad. The rest of you were not at this level, and Ben is 21 points behind in second.
stinker: Brahmes, 28 points. That is the lowest score in the league and 52 behind Asher. Kudus, Sávio and Doku all scored nothing, and Kinsky conceded 3 in a Spurs defeat. Rogers made 8, which was the high point of the week. It was a short list.
bench: Josh and Jack, 10 points left on the bench each. Josh left Trafford on the bench. Trafford kept a clean sheet for Leeds, made 3 saves and scored 9. Jack left Muharemović there for 6 points. Both are doing well in the table, but they should check the team sheet.
bench_jam: Jonny. Amad did not play, so Dewsbury-Hall came on and scored 11. He scored, kept a clean sheet and took 3 bonus for Everton. That is a decent swap for a man who had dropped Dorgu for Amad this week. Jonny sits third.
red_card: Jonny, for Cash. The Aston Villa defender lost 1 point after Brighton scored 4 against Villa. He also picked up a yellow card. Cash played the full 90 minutes, so he had plenty of time to do it. Jonny recovered through Dewsbury-Hall, but this one will be remembered.
gloves: Brahmes, for Lammens. The Man Utd keeper scored 1 point, conceded 2 and made 2 saves in a 2-0 defeat at Hull. He was on the same team as Cunha, who made 2 and conceded the same. Brahmes needed everything to go right and nothing did.

xi.385: Trafford kept a clean sheet for Leeds and scored 9. Josh left him on the bench. The team of the week noticed, and Josh probably did too.
xi.115: De Cuyper scored 17, the best score of the week. Asher owns him, and the table reflects it.
xi.10: White got an assist and a clean sheet for Arsenal, and scored 11. Asher again.
xi.388: Guéhi scored for Man City and made 10. Louie owns him, so some good came of the week.
xi.154: Palmer scored and assisted for Chelsea and made 13. Ben's best player, which explains why he is second.
xi.335: Stach scored for Leeds, kept a clean sheet and made 13. Jack's best score, and he had 16 defensive contributions too.
xi.367: Gakpo scored in the 2-2 draw at Newcastle and made 12. Asher owns him as well, naturally.
xi.15: Ødegaard scored for Arsenal and made 11 in 75 minutes. Jonny's second-best performer.
xi.236: Dewsbury-Hall scored 11 for Everton after coming on for Amad. Jonny's bench was better than most people's team.
xi.165: João Pedro scored and assisted for Chelsea and made 11. Josh is happy with that, even if the bench stayed busy.
xi.316: Emersonn scored for Ipswich and made 9 in 65 minutes. Louie brought him in on waivers this week, which looks fine.
